intended_object: The equivalence relation on the disjoint union of two copies of the square [-1,1]×[-1,1] that glues the right side (re = 1) of the first copy to the right side of the second copy, matching points with the same imaginary part. Its quotient is two squares glued along a common side. Source: the docstring and the neighbouring `SeamGenerator` and `SquareGluing`.
explanation:
The definition is `Relation.EqvGen.setoid SeamGenerator`, the equivalence relation generated by a seam relation. `SeamGenerator` relates `inl z` to `inr w` exactly when `z.re = 1`, `w.re = 1` and `z.im = w.im`, which is point-for-point gluing of the two distinguished sides. Taking the reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure gives the standard equivalence relation used to glue two squares along a common edge, so the definition matches its docstring.

The library also proves that the relation does what it should. Merging the two squares into one large square (`squarePairMerge`) is constant on equivalence classes, and two points of the disjoint union have the same image under the merge only if they are related. So the relation makes no unintended identifications.

The object is specific by design, and Mathlib has no general version that would make this too narrow. It is a concrete step in the classification-of-surfaces proof (two disks glued along a boundary arc form a disk), so one could also see it as an internal device.
